0.original: Linyeve, a quartermaster at Hyrstmill, needs an adventurer to bring her a glimshroom, a variety of brightly glowing fungus.

1.original: Pick a glimshroom from the rock face in the southwest of Peacegarden. Linyeve insists that you harvest the fungus with the brightest glow.

2.original: Deliver the glimshroom to Linyeve at Hyrstmill.

3.original: Glimshrooms are an essential ingredient in the medicine used to treat the disease known as the Creeping Death. With so few conjurers present in Hyrstmill, Linyeve prefers to keep a supply of the medicine on hand to deal with possible outbreaks.

25.original: Deliver the glimshroom to Linyeve at Hyrstmill.

48.original: You have the look of an adventurer! Adventurers love little tasks, do they not? Well, I need you to head into the forest and pick a glimshroom for me.

49.original: You...haven't the faintest idea what a glimshroom is, do you? “Glimshroom” is the common name for a variety of fungus with a unique white phosphorescence. Hm? What did you say? “A glowing mushroom”? ...Yes, I suppose you could put it that way. There is a colony on the rock face in the southwest of Peacegarden.

50.original: But do not simply pick the first one you come across! The brightest “glowing mushroom” you can find, if you please!

51.original: Hm? Well, yes, I would love to be able to harvest glimshrooms for myself, but there is the small matter of Ixali scouts. Not terribly friendly, those chaps. Off you go, then!

52.original: Were you able to find the glimshrooms?

53.original: Ah, would you look at that glow! Perfect! This will help me mix a potent remedy for the Creeping Death.

54.original: To forestall the obvious question, the Creeping Death is a deadly plague that once ravaged the Hyuran population of Gridania. Though it can now be cured through simple conjury, it doesn't hurt to have a ready supply of the medicine.

55.original: After all, out here in Hyrstmill, we cannot always rely on a conjurer to be on hand whenever a youngling coughs. Thank the Matron for wandering adventurers, though, hm?
